problem: Omnidirectional (equirectangular) observations could give wide coverage for EM-EQA, but equirectangular distortion degrades VLM recognition and the wide field of view adds irrelevant background and visual-token burden. Prior EQA work mostly assumes perspective images or explicit 3D memory, and pretrained BLIP-2 retrieval is unreliable on omnidirectional inputs.
motivation: Omnidirectional cameras could remove the need for explicit rotation actions and improve memory coverage, but only if VLMs can use them effectively. Feeding raw equirectangular images to a VLM hurts accuracy, and naive relevance retrieval on cubemap faces picks irrelevant or redundant views. So the paper needs a question-conditioned, diversity-aware way to choose a few informative perspective views.
key_idea: Convert each equirectangular image into six cubemap perspective views, score them with a BLIP-2 ITM head fine-tuned on filtered VQAv2 with supervised contrastive loss, and pick a few views by a diversity-aware greedy selection (relevance-ranked with a similarity constraint) to feed a VLM.
insight: Fine-tuning the relevance model is the critical ingredient: cubemap with pretrained BLIP-2 drops to 41.7 (vs 49.9 for raw equirectangular top-K), but with fine-tuning it reaches 55.2, and diversity-aware selection adds a further 2.3 to reach 57.5. Treating visual similarity as a constraint on a preserved relevance ranking beats the weighted MMR objective (best 55.8) and a caption-based R-EQA-style selector (50.3). Omnidirectional histories are also much less sensitive to removing rotation views (57.9→55.9) than perspective ones (61.1→45.5).
method: Cubemap projection: backward-samples each 2048x1024 equirectangular image into six perspective faces (Front/Back/Left/Right/Top/Bottom) via spherical coordinates, giving 6T candidate views.

Fine-tuned BLIP-2 relevance: the ITM score is the match-minus-mismatch logit. It is fine-tuned with LoRA (r=16, α=32) on the Q-Former plus a full ITM head, with the image encoder and queries frozen. Training data is VQAv2 with generic questions filtered by an LLM (441K questions remain).
Supervised contrastive ITM loss: image-question pairs sharing identical question text are treated as positives within a mini-batch, with a symmetric i2t/t2i loss.
Score-based partitioning: candidates are split by ITM score threshold γ=0.1 into high- and low-confidence sets, so low-relevance views are not chosen merely for diversity.

Diversity-Aware Greedy Selection: iterate the high set in descending score order and accept a view only if its max cosine similarity to already selected views (mean of the 32 BLIP-2 query embeddings) is below τ=0.97, until K views are selected.
Fallbacks: fill from rejected high candidates, then from the low set with the diversity constraint; if no candidate reaches γ, use uniform temporal sampling.
Answering: the K selected perspective images (K in 1..10, no resizing) go to Qwen2-VL-72B-Instruct, evaluated with LLM-Match (gpt-4-turbo).

setting.backbone: Fine-tuned BLIP-2 (ITM, LoRA) as selector + Qwen2-VL-72B-Instruct (frozen) as answer model
setting.model_size: Qwen2-VL-72B answerer; BLIP-2 selector with LoRA rank 16
setting.training_data: BLIP-2 ITM fine-tuned on VQAv2 (443K image-question pairs, 82K images; 441K after removing generic questions); the answer VLM is not trained
setting.observation: Equirectangular RGB 2048x1024 rendered along OpenEQA HM3D trajectories (also standard perspective 1920x1080 for comparison)
setting.action_space: none (episodic memory QA on recorded trajectories; no navigation)
setting.simulator: Habitat-Matterport 3D (OpenEQA HM3D episodes; equirectangular rendered from meshes)
setting.privileged: Recorded agent positions and orientations from OpenEQA used to render equirectangular images; otherwise none

results: On the OpenEQA HM3D EM-EQA subset, the method reaches 57.9 LLM-Match with equirectangular observations, beating Multi-Frame VLMs (54.5) and RAG with BLIP (50.4 / 44.3 cubemap). Without rotation views (65.5% fewer frames) it keeps 55.9 versus 52.6 for the best baseline. It also beats the baselines with other answer models, e.g. GPT-5.6 Sol 66.6 vs 56.9.
limitations: Selects views independently, so it cannot model temporal order, room connectivity, counting, absence checks or multi-view integration (e.g. a route-following failure case).
Selection is slow (25.2 s vs 8.4 s for multi-frame at K=5 in the Original setting), and fixed cube faces can split objects at face boundaries.
Evaluated only on the HM3D subset of OpenEQA, with only BLIP-2 as relevance model and no real robot.
